title: A Lost Megalodon Fossil Hints at a 79-Foot Shark

scenes.text: Megalodon may have been seventy-nine feet long.
The proof is a set of giant bones found in Denmark.
They are vertebrae, nine inches across.
They are the biggest shark vertebrae ever found.
The fossils vanished in 1989 and were thought destroyed.
Decades later, a few turned up on a museum shelf.
Scientists say that shark might have been almost two buses long.

description:
Megalodon may have been seventy-nine feet long.
A new study of rediscovered vertebrae from Denmark suggests a shark up to 79 feet, though the estimate is uncertain and rests on one animal.
Would you swim in the ocean if it were still alive?
first_comment: Bonus: the authors call about 80 feet the largest scientifically justifiable estimate. Do you think megalodon was that big?
